title: cursor-prefetch-sdks: resilient streaming iterator for embeddings + rerank
creator: Alyssa Chen
description:
Goal: implement a unified, ergonomic streaming/paginated iterator in Python/TypeScript/Go SDKs that provides robust prefetching, backpressure awareness, and retry semantics for the embeddings and rerank endpoints. This ticket focuses on API parity and ship-ready examples + tests.

Motivation:
- Many customers sacrifice throughput for latency because existing helpers either fetch large pages up front or provide very low-level pagination primitives.
- We need a single mental model across SDKs: a lazy iterator that optionally prefetches N pages, knows when requests are idempotent, and supports graceful cancellation and retry-on-transient-failure.

Acceptance criteria:
1) SDK surface: Python, TypeScript, and Go expose a similarly-named iterator (Python: EmbeddingIterator, TS: createEmbeddingStream, Go: EmbeddingStream) that supports:
   - next()/async iteration (Python/TS) and channel-based receive (Go)
   - configurable prefetch window (integer) and max inflight requests
   - early termination / cancel API that cleans up in-flight requests
   - deterministic retry policy for transient 5xx / network errors with exponential backoff and jitter
2) Rerank behavior: iterator supports batched "rerank()" calls where each item is paired with score metadata; iterator ensures ordering and at-most-once semantics for user callbacks.
3) Backpressure: TS and Python async implementations must pause prefetching when consumer is slow; Go stream honors context cancellation.
4) Tests: unit tests that simulate partial page failures and validate retries, e2e integration test against staging runtime showing no duplicates and correct ordering.
5) Docs/examples: idiomatic example for each SDK demonstrating streaming embeddings for a long corpus, handling transient errors, and using cancelation.
6) Benchmarks: a simple benchmark comparing no-prefetch vs prefetch=2 for 1M tokens workload; prefetch should improve throughput >= 20% with <5% median latency increase.
7) Release: included in sdk-2025.03 release with migration notes.

Design notes / decisions:
- Cursor vs offset: use server-provided opaque cursor tokens instead of offsets to support variable-sized pages and future server-side optimizations.
- Prefetch window default = 1 (no speculative fetch) to preserve latency; allow SDK config to set to 2-4 for throughput-sensitive workloads.
- Retry semantics: only retry idempotent fetches (pagination cursors are idempotent). For rerank streaming where items cause side-effects (e.g., user-provided scoring hooks), provide explicit at_most_once config that uses server-side dedup tokens when available.
- Backpressure implementation: Python/TS will implement producer-consumer queues sized by prefetch window; TS will use ReadableStream for browser-friendly streaming and async iterators for node. Go will use buffered channels with selectable cancellation.
- Telemetry: emit metrics per SDK for prefetch_inflight, retry_count, page_latency_ms; wire into Console SDK telemetry hooks so Console can surface token-level cost for streaming routes.

API sketches (examples):
- Python (async):
  from redwood import EmbeddingsClient
  it = EmbeddingsClient().stream_embeddings(corpus_ids, prefetch=2, retry_policy="adaptive")
  async for item in it:
      process(item.vector)
      if need_stop: it.cancel()

- TypeScript (node):
  const client = new RedwoodEmbeddings();
  const stream = client.createEmbeddingStream(corpusIds, { prefetch: 2 });
  for await (const item of stream) {
    handle(item.vector);
    if (shouldStop) { stream.cancel(); break; }
  }

- Go:
  ctx, cancel := context.WithCancel(context.Background())
  ch := client.StreamEmbeddings(ctx, corpusIds, EmbeddingStreamOptions{Prefetch:2})
  for item := range ch {
    process(item.Vector)
    if cond { cancel(); break }
  }

Rollout plan:
- Implement core logic in Python + TS first (most used by PLG customers), run internal dogfood + integration tests.
- Add Go parity after API finalized.
- Feature-flagged behavior defaulting to prefetch=1; enable prefetch=2 via opt-in flag and surface suggestions in Optimize.

Backward compatibility:
- Existing pagination helpers (cursor-based list_pages helpers) continue to exist; new streaming iterator is additive with migration guide.

Security / compliance:
- No new secrets stored. All network retries respect existing KMS/HSM policies; library does not cache sensitive payloads beyond in-memory buffers.

Testing plan:
- Unit: retry injection harness that simulates 50% 5xx on page 2; assert at-most-once yield and final success.
- Integration: run against staging runtime with injected delays to validate backpressure.
- Perf: synthetic corpus (100k items) benchmark with prefetch 0/1/2/4.

Notes for engineers:
- Be careful with GC in Go when using buffered channels and contexts; ensure no goroutine leaks on cancel.
- Ensure SDK user-visible timeout semantics are consistent with client-level timeout config (not service-level).
- Keep buffer sizes small to avoid token cost spikes and OOM on large corpora.
comments: 2025-01-10 Alyssa Chen: Created ticket. Initial API sketches and acceptance criteria. Filed as cross-sdk effort; suggested order: Python -> TS -> Go.

2025-01-14 Diego Morales: Spike completed for Python async iterator. Prototype uses asyncio.Queue with prefetch window and passes basic cancellation tests. Observed ~28% throughput improvement with prefetch=2 in small benchmark (50k items). Pushed experimental branch: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/3124
2025-01-20 Priya Gupta (QA): Added test plan notes. Will add failure injection harness to CI to simulate transient 5xx on pagination requests.

2025-01-25 Design review (Ehsan K.): Reviewed UX for TS ReadableStream API; recommended exposing both ReadableStream and async iterator for node/browser compatibility. Also requested explicit examples for Deno and bun runtimes.

2025-01-30 Diego Morales: Added TypeScript prototype implementing ReadableStream + for-await. Found race where cancel + in-flight retry caused duplicate yields in 1/2000 runs; fixed by attaching monotonic request IDs and dedup map in iterator state. Patch: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/3158

2025-02-02 Alyssa Chen: Updated acceptance criteria to require telemetry keys and added release target sdk-2025.03. Added dependency on ENG-70321 (adaptive-chunking helpers) for shared batching logic. Marking as In Progress and coordinating Go implementation start next week.
